Fixed. The bug was in `display_name()` (`app/display.py:1-4`): it force-encoded names to UTF-8 then decoded as `ascii` with `errors="ignore"`, silently dropping every non-Latin byte — so any Arabic (or other non-Latin script) name collapsed to an empty string. `.title()` doesn't need ASCII to work correctly, so the ASCII round-trip was unnecessary.

**Fix**: truncate by character count and title-case directly, no encoding detour:
```python
def display_name(name, limit=24):
    return name.strip()[:limit].title()
```
Verified `display_name("أحمد")` now returns `"أحمد"` unchanged (Arabic has no case, so `.title()` is a no-op on it). Added a regression test; full suite is 6/6 passing.
